privacy_html:
1. Controller

NXplosion Labs (Duk3X), independent developer based in Spain.
Contact: duk3x.dev@gmail.com

2. What the app does

Platinum Hunter shows the trophies of your PlayStation Network account. Most of it runs only on your device, which communicates with Sony's servers. The community features (Hunter Level and rankings, friends, chat, groups, tips, ratings and cloud backup) use our server, hosted on Google Firebase (Google Cloud, European Union region, Belgium). They are only turned on if you verify your account in the app.

3. Data that stays on your device

  • PSN credentials: you enter your username and password only on Sony's official page. The app never sees or stores them.
  • PSN session: session tokens are stored encrypted on your device, with a key protected by the Android Keystore, to keep you signed in.
  • Trophy and game cache, settings and exports: stored on your device. Files you export go wherever you choose.
  • PlayStation messages: the app reads and sends your PSN messages directly with Sony from your device; they don't go through our server. Which chats you've read is stored only on your device.
  • Background checks: if you turn on alerts, your device checks your trophies (every few hours) and your PSN message inbox (every 15 minutes) with Sony, and lets you know with local notifications. You can turn this off in Profile › Notifications.
  • Critic scores: once a week the app downloads from our website a public list of OpenCritic scores taken from Wikidata. It doesn't send any of your data.
  • Widgets and shortcuts: they show data that's already on your device (your level, platinums, latest trophy and the game you're playing).

4. Data processed by our server

Only if you verify your account (Home › Hunter Level):

  • Verification and Hunter Level: the app sends your PSN session token to the server over HTTPS. It is used at that moment to confirm that the account is yours and to read your trophies from Sony, and it is not stored. Along with those trophies, we store your online ID, your avatar, your PSN account's country, your points, level and trophy counts, your progress in each game, the hours the app estimates you took for each platinum (used only for the “Platinum in” average, without showing who) and signals to detect impossible trophies (for example, hundreds in the same second).
  • Public catalogue: names, icons and rarity of each game's trophies. It doesn't identify anyone.
  • What you post: tips, votes, game ratings (difficulty, hours and score), reviews, “Can it no longer be earned?” votes, chat and group messages, the groups you create or join, and invitations.
  • Community safety: the reports you send or receive and the people you block.
  • Alerts: a Firebase Cloud Messaging notification identifier to send you chat and group alerts, if you turn them on.
  • Cloud backup: your hunt list, your wishlist, the trophies you mark as unobtainable and your appearance settings, so you can restore them when you change phones.

Your online ID, avatar, level, points and country are visible to other users in the rankings and in the community. Your chat messages are only seen by the people in the chat or group.

5. Advertising (Google AdMob)

The free version shows ads from Google AdMob. Google may collect the device's advertising ID, IP address (approximate location), device information and ad interaction data to show ads, measure them and prevent fraud. In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, the app asks for your consent before showing personalised ads, and you can change it at any time from the Privacy and ads menu. More information: How Google uses data. You can reset or delete your advertising ID in Android settings.

6. Crash reports (Firebase Crashlytics)

If the app closes because of an error, it sends a report to Firebase Crashlytics so we can fix it: the phone model, the Android and app version, the time of the crash, the part of the code where it happened and a random installation identifier. It doesn't include your PSN account, your trophies or your messages. It is kept for up to 90 days.

7. Purchases

Premium purchases and subscriptions are handled by Google Play. We don't receive your payment details.

8. Legal basis

  • Performance of the service you request: showing your trophies and, if you verify your account, the community features.
  • Legitimate interest in keeping the community safe and the rankings fair (cheat detection, reports and blocks).
  • Your consent for personalised advertising and alerts (which you can withdraw at any time).

9. Retention and deletion

Server data is kept for as long as you use the community features. You can delete it whenever you like in Profile › Delete my server data, or request deletion by email at the address in section 1, giving your PSN online ID. We will reply within 30 days at most.

Deleted: your ranking and progress, your cloud backup, your reviews, tips, ratings and playtime, your votes, your chats and the groups you created (with their messages), your blocks and your server account.

Kept: what you wrote in other people's groups, anonymous and hidden; the reports you made, without who made them, so the same thing can't be reported twice; and group bans, so that deleting your account can't be used to get around them. Crashlytics crash reports are deleted automatically after 90 days.

Deleting your data doesn't cancel a Premium subscription: that is done in Google Play. Signing out deletes the tokens and the cache from your device, and uninstalling the app removes all its local data.

10. Processors and transfers

We use Google (Firebase, Cloud Functions, Cloud Messaging, Crashlytics, AdMob and Google Play) as a data processor. Server data is stored in the European Union. Google may process some data outside the EU under the safeguards of the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.

11. Minors

The app is not intended for children under 16.

12. Your rights

You can exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction of processing and data portability by writing to duk3x.dev@gmail.com, and lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency, Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (aepd.es).

13. Disclaimer

Platinum Hunter is an independent app by NXplosion Labs, not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment. PlayStation, PlayStation Network, PS5, PS4, PS3 and PS Vita are registered trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. Game and trophy names and images belong to their respective owners.

rules_html:
Platinum Hunter community guidelines

Tips, reviews and ratings are read by trophy hunters all over the world. To post, you have to accept these guidelines.

  1. Respect. No insults, harassment, threats, discrimination or hate speech, and that includes against studios or players.
  2. Nothing inappropriate. No sexual or violent content, nothing that promotes illegal activities and nothing that could harm anyone.
  3. No spam or personal data. No advertising, no links to other sites and no personal data, yours or anyone else's (real name, phone number, address, accounts).
  4. Fair play. No faking trophies, cheating in the rankings, or buying, selling or sharing accounts or boosting services.
  5. Flag your spoilers. If a tip gives away the story, say so at the start.
  6. Write about the game. Tips are for earning trophies, and reviews are for talking about the game and its trophies.

What happens if they're broken

Anyone can report a tip, a review or a player. After 3 reports, the content is hidden automatically until we review it. If the guidelines are broken, we may delete what was posted and remove access to the community features, temporarily or permanently. We'll always tell you why.

If you disagree

Write to us at duk3x.dev@gmail.com and we'll look into it.

What you post

What you post is yours, but by posting it you give us permission to show it in the app. You can delete it whenever you like.
mc_privacy_html:
1. Controller

NXplosion Labs (Duk3X), independent developer based in Spain.
Contact: duk3x.dev@gmail.com

2. What the app does

Moodcell: Emoji Battery puts a character or a design where the battery goes and lets you customise your phone's status bar (clock, centre, battery, icons and background), along with live wallpapers and a widget. It has no accounts and no server of its own: everything you set up stays on your device.

3. Data that stays on your device

  • Battery: the app reads from Android the level, whether it is charging, voltage, current, power, temperature, charge, cycles, health, chemistry and charger type, to draw the bar, the panel and the charging animation. The graph of the last 5 minutes exists only in the phone's memory.
  • Your settings: the design, the parts, the theme, the colours, your favourites and the apps where you hide the bar are stored on the device.
  • Your background photo: if you choose a photo from your gallery as the background, it is copied inside the app so it can be drawn. It never leaves the device and is not included in backups.
  • Android backup: if you have it turned on, Android may save your Moodcell settings to your Google account so you can restore them when you change phones. This is managed by Google, and you control it in Android settings.

4. Accessibility service

Moodcell uses the Android accessibility service only so that it can show its bar on top of the status bar and hide it when needed. With it, the app reads which app is in front and the type and size of its window, to hide the bar in full screen and in the apps you choose, and detects when you tap the bar so it can open the part you tapped. It does not read what you type or the content of your screen, does not store that information and does not send it anywhere. You can turn it off whenever you like in Android's accessibility settings.

5. Location (RF mode only)

The optional RF mode draws signal coverage like a spectrum analyser. To read mobile network information (signal and cells), Android requires the location permission. Moodcell uses it only at that moment, to draw the bar while that mode is active: it does not store your location or send it. If you don't turn on RF mode, the app doesn't ask for this permission.

6. Advertising (Google AdMob)

The free version may show ads from Google AdMob. Google may collect the device's advertising ID, IP address (approximate location), device information and ad interaction data to show ads, measure them and prevent fraud. In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, the app asks for your consent before showing personalised ads, and you can change it at any time from the app's settings. More information: How Google uses data. You can reset or delete your advertising ID in Android settings.

7. Purchases

The Premium purchase is handled by Google Play. We don't receive your payment details.

8. Legal basis

  • Performance of the service you request: customising your bar, your wallpapers and your widget.
  • Your consent for the accessibility service, location in RF mode and personalised advertising (which you can withdraw at any time).

9. Retention and deletion

As there is no server and there are no accounts, we don't keep any of your data. To delete everything related to Moodcell, just clear the app's data in Android settings or uninstall it. If you have any questions, write to us at the address in section 1.

10. Processors and transfers

We use Google (AdMob and Google Play) as a data processor for advertising and purchases. Google may process some data outside the European Union under the safeguards of the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.

11. Minors

Moodcell is suitable for everyone: it has no accounts, chats or content from other users, and we don't collect personal data from anyone.

If you are under the age of digital consent in your country (14 in Spain), ask a parent or guardian to decide about personalized ads. You can decline them in the consent notice or in the app's settings; the ads you see will then not be personalized.

12. Your rights

You can exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction of processing and data portability by writing to duk3x.dev@gmail.com, and lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency, Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (aepd.es).

13. Changes

If this policy changes, we will publish the new version on this page with its date.
